For this design, use category-stratified paired user bootstrapping: retain each user’s two binary hit@10 outcomes on identical candidates; define d(c,u)=hitA−hitB and Δ=(1/4)Σc mean_u d(c,u). Independently within each category, resample 200 user pairs with replacement, recompute Δ, and repeat 10,000 times; report Δ and its 2.5th–97.5th percentile interval, alongside category differences and discordant-pair counts. Pairing preserves covariance; fixed category sizes preserve macro weighting. This applies the [paired-bootstrap principle](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html) to the specified benchmark. Aggregate HR values alone cannot recover paired uncertainty; user-level outputs are required.

Repeatedly choosing checkpoints or configurations using these same validation users creates winner’s-curse optimism. Bootstrapping only the selected predictors does not account for selection, so intervals excluding zero are exploratory rather than confirmatory evidence after adaptive search. Report the selection rule and number of checkpoints/configurations inspected; preserve the untouched host test for final assessment. Existing validation outputs alone cannot provide an unbiased independent evaluation of the adaptive search. [Cawley and Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html) explain this model-selection bias.

With training seed 42 alone, intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on the fitted checkpoints, histories, four categories, and fixed candidate lists, assuming users are independent within categories. They cannot estimate initialization/minibatch variability or establish expected superiority across training runs; shared seeds do not eliminate that limitation. [Benchmark-variance research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.03098) distinguishes these uncertainty sources. For the exact fixed validation panel, Δ itself is deterministic. Fixed-negative uncertainty also remains unmeasured, and sampled HR rankings need not match full-catalog rankings ([sampled-metrics study](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). All proposed calculations postprocess existing outputs without changing evaluation or training additional models.
